chunks: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, "Who carries out the hudud: the ruler or the judge?" He said, "The implementation of the hudud belongs to the one to whom judgment belongs."

key_terms.إِقَامَةُ الْحُدُودِ: The enforcement and execution of prescribed legal punishments.
key_terms.الْحُدُودَ: The prescribed legal punishments set by the Sacred Law.
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: Judicial authority or the power to issue binding judgment.
key_terms.الْقَاضِي: The judge who exercises judicial function.

ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to carry out hudud in Islamic law: the ruler or the judge?
ai.summary: This hadith states that carrying out the hudud is the responsibility of the one who possesses judicial authority. It links the enforcement of legal punishments to legitimate authority in judgment, making it a key text in discussions of legal and governmental jurisdiction in fiqh.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5135 - Sulayman ibn Dawud Al-Minqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), "Who is responsible for carrying out the legal punishments (hudud) -the ruler or the judge?"
Imam (as) replied: "The implementation of the legal punishments belongs to the one who holds the authority of judgment."
